# E9 — PLISM external validation on the rebuilt core grid

**Status:** results from the cohort rebuild of 2026-08-22/23
**Contract:** [`e9_plism_native_ert_contract.md`](e9_plism_native_ert_contract.md), Amendment 3
**Report:** `presentations/pannormal_plism_2026-08-23/index.html`, Part IV
**Generated by:** `src/build_e9_core_results.py` from the analysis outputs

This replaces the sparse-sampling PLISM arm. The locked outputs of that arm are
untouched and still on disk under their original names; everything here lives
under `outputs/plism_core_*`.

## 1. What the cohort is now

|  | Sparse arm | Core grid |
|---|---:|---:|
| Locations measured | 3,816 | **116,831** |
| Scanner-to-reference measurements | 26,712 | **817,817** |
| Tissue coverage, same footprint measure | 2.9 % | **88.2 %** |
| TMA cores | position index | **46 published tissue names** |
| SQ file correction | not applied | **applied** |
| Encoders | E0: ResNet50, UNI v1, CONCH v1, Virchow2 | **E9: UNI2-h, CONCHv1.5, H-optimus-1** |

Alignment on the rebuilt grid: median residual
0.091–0.113 µm per scanner over
700,986 non-reference measurements, 99.57 %
clearing the 1 µm gate. The canvas fit recovers the Hamamatsu pitch independently on every
section at 0.2188–0.2219 µm/unit, with rotation within
3.25° of zero and mask Dice 0.82–0.86.

`response` is stored per location but not gated on. With the SQ files corrected, the leak it
was aimed at — a location clearing the residual gate while the alignment could not be verified
— is 0.70 % of non-reference measurements. Amendment 2's per-patch
`response >= 0.3` recommendation is withdrawn; see Amendment 3.

| `SQ` | 0.805 | 1.543 | — |
| `AT2` | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |

Rank correlation with the locked ordering over the 4 shared scanners:
**raw -1.000**, **after Reinhard +0.800**. The out-of-focus `HRH/S60` block is
excluded from these; with it in, S60 reads 0.613 raw and
1.463 after Reinhard, and nothing else moves.

### The three-term decomposition does not survive

Running the contrast audit — raw fine-band power divided by the squared optical-density spread
— on both cohorts:

| Cohort | GT450 raw fine band vs AT2 | Predicted by contrast | Excess |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PLISM (807,536 locations) | 0.307 | 0.220 | **1.40×** |
| PanNormal | 0.293 | 0.215 | **1.36×** |

The August edition put PLISM's excess at 0.90× and concluded that equalising sampling removes
it, which supported splitting GT450's advantage into roughly half optics and half sampling
density. It does not remove it. What survives is that raw band power is dominated by contrast,
which is the mechanism behind the hinge in section 12 of the report.

Over the shared scanners the contrast-normalised residual reproduces the locked ordering on
PanNormal (+1.000) but not on PLISM
(+0.200).

## 4. Feature space (chance for the probe is 0.143)

| Model | CORAL | CORAL probe | Procrustes | Procrustes probe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UNI2-h | +10.6 % | 0.036 | +30.5 % | 0.048 |
| CONCHv1.5 | +12.0 % | 0.075 | +12.5 % | 0.119 |
| H-optimus-1 | +18.3 % | 0.040 | +31.2 % | 0.064 |

All 6 of 6 feature-space conditions are safe and improved. The
August edition's qualification — CORAL fails for the highest-dimensional encoders — does not
reproduce.

### CORAL sample-size sweep

| Model | dim | Smallest fit, samples/dim | Radius reduction | Full fit, samples/dim | Radius reduction | Crosses zero at |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UNI2-h | 1536 | 0.16 | -71.1 % | 68 | **+10.6 %** | 32.5 |
| CONCHv1.5 | 768 | 0.31 | -287.1 % | 34 | **+12.0 %** | 6.5 |
| H-optimus-1 | 1536 | 0.16 | -117.0 % | 68 | **+18.3 %** | 32.5 |

The x quantity already divides by the embedding dimension, so a constant "n samples per
parameter" requirement would put the crossings together. It does not: the 768-dimensional
encoder breaks even at 6.5 samples per dimension and
both 1536-dimensional encoders at 32.5. **The break-even
has to be measured per encoder**, which costs one refit sweep on features that already exist.

|---|---:|---:|---:|

### Does the stain's own darkness predict the scanner's spectral slope?

| Scanner | β | z | Section variance explained | Folds significant | Leave-one-section-out |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `GT450` | -0.002 | -0.18 | — | 0 / 12 | — |
| `S210` | -0.104 | -3.03 | 43 % | 11 / 12 | breaks without `HR` |
| `S60` | -0.076 | -1.24 | — | 1 / 12 | — |
| `Philips` | +0.063 | +4.04 | 61 % | 11 / 12 | breaks without `HR` |
| `S360` | -0.067 | -8.57 | 89 % | 12 / 12 | **stable** |
| `SQ` | -0.043 | -0.60 | — | 0 / 12 | — |

1 of 6 survive every fold. The August edition ran this check by hand on
one scanner and concluded that staining condition is a label rather than an explanatory
variable; for `S360` it is an explanatory variable, and the check is now in
`analyze_plism_stain_covariate.py --leave-one-out`. The section that breaks the other two is
`HR`, which is also the section three standard deviations darker than any other and the only
one where the feature-space corrections of section 4 do nothing.

## 6. Tissue

Top-1 retrieval across scanners, pooled over all sections, runs from
0.559 to
1.000
across the 46 named tissue types. The bottom is
liver, skeletal muscle, collagenous fibre and left ventricle; the top is gallbladder, bronchus,
colonic adenocarcinoma and ileum. The match fails where the tissue has least architecture to
anchor it.

Mean top-1 against AT2 per encoder: UNI2-h 0.911, CONCHv1.5 0.921, H-optimus-1 0.960. Encoder rank agreement on which scanner is hardest: CONCHv1.5/H-optimus-1 +0.94; CONCHv1.5/UNI2-h +0.43; H-optimus-1/UNI2-h +0.26.

## 7. Reproduction

    sbatch scripts/plism_core_population_array.sbatch
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_psd_array.sbatch
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_reinhard_array.sbatch
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_render_bands_array.sbatch
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_gainfit.sbatch
    bash   scripts/plism_core_submit_conditions.sh
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_arma_analysis.sbatch
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_covariate_folds.sbatch
    python scripts/_aggregate_covariate_folds.py
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_featcorr.sbatch
    sbatch scripts/plism_core_pfm_frontier.sbatch
    python src/build_pannormal_plism_report.py

Integrity: `scripts/_verify_conditions.py` checks all 2,177,672 condition vectors against the
checkpoint contract, for finiteness, and for sitting on exactly the frozen evaluation grid.
